I am 63 this year. I never went to school, not one day. I started following my mother to the fields when I was 13, so I have been farming for 50 years. My land is small, only 4.1 mu, just me and my old man at home. We have a well, so water is not a big worry, but every bag of fertilizer costs real money, so I count it out carefully.

For wheat, I do what I did last year. Before planting in October, I spread one big bag — about 100 jin — of that three-number fertilizer on each mu. The shop calls it 15-15-15. That is four bags for my whole field. Then the rotary tiller comes and churns it into the soil. In March when the wheat turns green, I spread another 15 jin of white urea on each mu. I would rather put a little too much than too little. A bad harvest means no money for the whole year; wasting a bit of fertilizer is just a few yuan lost. I irrigate three times: once when it wakes up, once when it grows tall, and once when the grains are filling. I spray twice — once for weeds in spring, once for bugs when it heads. My neighbor Wang's family does the same, and they got about 900 jin per mu last year. I expect the same.

For corn, I plant right after the wheat comes off in June. I put down one big bag of 15-15-15 per mu again, but corn eats more nitrogen, so when the plants are knee-high I add 20 jin of urea per mu. The rotary tiller works the ground after wheat harvest. I irrigate twice if the rain does not come — once when it is shooting up, and once when the ears are filling. I spray twice, for weeds and for that stem borer worm. If the weather holds, I should get 1,000 jin per mu. I do not hire labor; it is just the two of us. I do not try new tricks. I watch what others do, and I stick to what I know.
